speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation, could you please describe the specific movements you are experiencing and when they first started?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are feeling better mentally since starting risperidone, but I need to clarify the movement disorder. Are you experiencing stiffness, tremors, or an inability to sit still?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: That description of restlessness and pacing is classic for akathisia. Have you noticed these symptoms worsening at any specific time of day, such as after taking your morning dose of risperidone?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: The absence of substance use and other medical history strongly supports a medication-induced etiology. Given your history of starting risperidone and the classic symptoms of inner restlessness and pacing, I am confident in my assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Akathisia
